objects.name: Chipkin Example B-EC
objects.note: the device itself; the instance is configurable with --deviceID. The stack rows are device-wide facts only the stack knows - the protocol version and revision it implements, the services and object types it was configured with, the live object list and address-binding table. The accepted rows are the stack's configured defaults for APDU limits, segmentation, system status and database revision; an application that answered them from its own constants could contradict the stack, so this example does not

objects.name: Bronze
objects.note: REAL, degrees Celsius; starts at 21.5. F-COVM: Present_Value AND Status_Flags are both marked subscribable (SetPropertySubscribable), so a SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple naming both fires one multi-property notification when the up/down keys nudge this value

objects.name: Chartreuse
objects.note: F-OUTPUTS (NEW vs B-EM; canonical pattern from B-SA-CPP). REAL setpoint, 16-slot Priority_Array + Relinquish_Default (20.0); commandable. Present_Value itself is resolved by the stack from the Priority_Array - this application's Get callback answers the individual array-index reads (and Relinquish_Default) rather than Present_Value directly, exactly as B-SA's canonical pattern documents

objects.name: Fuchsia
objects.note: F-OUTPUTS (NEW vs B-EM). Active/inactive, commandable; Relinquish_Default inactive (0). Out-of-range writes (anything but 0/1) are rejected with value-out-of-range

objects.name: Indigo
objects.note: F-OUTPUTS (NEW vs B-EM). State 1..3, commandable; Relinquish_Default state 1. Out-of-range writes (state 0 or >3) are rejected with value-out-of-range. Verified by wire test: WriteProperty of state 9 rejected with value-out-of-range

objects.name: Vermilion
objects.note: BACnet/IP; Network_Type and Protocol_Level are set from BACnetStack_AddNetworkPortObject()'s arguments (IPv4, BACnet Application) at start-up, not a GetProperty callback like the object's other app-served rows; Changes_Pending is likewise computed and answered natively by the stack's Network Port object. Reliability has no fault condition this example detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal)

objects.name: Maroon
objects.note: F-ELEVATOR (canonical, from B-EM). Machine_Room_ID, Group_ID and Group_Members are NOT stack DEFAULTS - they are genuinely stored and served by BACnetStack_AddElevatorGroupObject (Group_Members is also maintained by BACnetStack_AddLiftOrEscalatorObject as Lift 1/Mauve is added to this group). They are marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic per-type table does not know about this object-specific host-configuration API and so cannot credit them as stack-served. isGroupOfLifts=true and supportLandingCallStatus=true: Group_Mode and LandingCalls are therefore also enabled (see the Lift's note for how the four F-ELEVATOR list/sequence callbacks are exercised) but property-profile-reference.md's generic Elevator Group table does not mark either 'required', so neither generates a checked row here - Group_Mode is served by GetPropertyEnumerated (normal) and LandingCalls by GetListElevatorGroupLandingCallStatus (the group's active landing calls, one element per call; an empty list returns false on the first call) regardless. NEW vs B-EM: Landing_Call_Control is writable - BACnetStack_RegisterCallbackSetElevatorGroupLandingCallControl is registered (B-EM deliberately leaves it unregistered) - and a landing call written to it is SERVED: the simulated car travels to the floor, opens its door, and the call leaves Landing_Calls (a destination call then becomes a car call). A call for a floor outside 1-8 is refused (the stack answers Error PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED: the callback has no errorCode parameter). The last accepted call reads back; before any it reads floor 0, direction none. Proven by tests/landing_call_test.py and landing_call_failure_test.py

objects.name: Mauve
objects.note: F-ELEVATOR (from B-EM). The Lift presents the car SIMULATION (simulation/ElevatorCar.cpp, the same file as B-EM's; README 'What is Simulation'): Car_Position and Car_Moving_Direction via GetPropertyUnsignedInteger/GetPropertyEnumerated, Car_Door_Status (one door, index 1) via GetPropertyEnumerated with useArrayIndex - SAFETY_LOCKED while the car moves, OPENING/OPENED/CLOSING/CLOSED at a stop - Passenger_Alarm and Out_Of_Service via GetPropertyBool, and Fault_Signals (DOOR_CLOSING_FAULT when a door fails to close) via GetListOfEnumerations. Every change goes to the stack with BACnetStack_UpdateValue. property-profile-reference.md's generated Lift table is INCOMPLETE relative to CASBACnetStackDLL.h's doc comment for BACnetStack_AddLiftOrEscalatorObject (a documentation gap in the stack repo, not a stack API gap): it omits those six required properties; this example serves them because clause 12.59 requires them. Status_Flags, Elevator_Group, Group_ID and Installation_ID ARE in the generic table (stack-computed/stack-stored) and are accepted for the same reason as Maroon's. Event reporting, both algorithms clause 12.59 names: CHANGE_OF_STATE on Passenger_Alarm (pAlarmValues TRUE; the 's' key or the test-only control channel presses the button) and FAULT_LISTED on Fault_Signals, both to Notification Class 1 (Crimson). Reliability is enabled for the fault algorithm and computed by the stack from it; the app does not serve it. Car_Position, Car_Moving_Direction and Car_Door_Status are SetPropertySubscribable (DS-COVM-B on the car). Optional Assigned_Landing_Calls (the group's active landing calls - Mauve is its only car - and none while the car is faulted), Registered_Car_Call (the car's pending stops that are not landing calls: a destination call's destination) and Landing_Door_Status (floors 1-8: the car's floor follows the car door, the others SAFETY_LOCKED) are enabled and served by the F-ELEVATOR sequence callbacks

objects.name: Mint
objects.note: F-ELEVATOR. Not a member of Maroon (a group of Lifts, isGroupOfLifts=true) - added with the spec's 'no reference' sentinel (4194303) for Elevator_Group, as clause 12.60.6 allows. Required Operation_Direction (no stack default), Passenger_Alarm and Out_Of_Service are served by the app; the optional Power_Mode and Escalator_Mode are enabled and served too, for a fuller demonstration. Status_Flags/Elevator_Group/Group_ID/Installation_ID are stack-stored, same reasoning as Mauve's

objects.name: Turquoise
objects.note: not one of the profile's named objects - added explicitly by this application, BEFORE Elevator Group 1 (Maroon), as the object Maroon's Machine_Room_ID references. BACnetStack_AddElevatorGroupObject's own doc comment reads as though the stack creates this object automatically if missing; verified against the running stack, it does not - AddElevatorGroupObject fails outright ('Create the Positive Integer Value object before adding the Elevator Group object') unless the application adds it first. Colour 'Turquoise' per docs/colour-table.md's global positive_integer_value mapping; Present_Value (required, no stack default) is served as an arbitrary plausible room id. Units defaults to no-units (accepted) since a machine-room identifier has none; Out_Of_Service is optional and left at the generic default

objects.name: Crimson
objects.note: AE-N-I-B / AE-ACK-B / AE-INFO-B. Priority, Ack_Required and Recipient_List are NOT stack DEFAULTS - they are genuinely populated by BACnetStack_AddNotificationClassObject (Priority, Ack_Required) and BACnetStack_AddRecipientToNotificationClass (Recipient_List) at start-up; marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic per-type table does not know about this object-specific host-configuration API. Unlike B-AAC (AE-CRL-B), Recipient_List is NOT made writable here - AE-CRL-B is not a required BIBB for this profile
